round: V3 · stopped here, at the owner's call
headline: Two structural faults fixed, the doors rebuilt from flat slabs into real six-panel doors, the stairwell reopened as a well, and the ceiling relit. Nine blind critics judged round 1 and lost every view; their verdicts are below and are what a next round would work from. Stopped here on the owner's call — the room is in a clean, consistent state.

p_runner.gap: The floor gives it away in two seconds. Ours is the darkest thing in the frame — roughly half the photograph's luminance, cool near-charcoal — where the real floor is a light greige that sits within about 15% of the wall grey and bounces light up onto the skirting. It also has no plank structure at all: no bevelled long edges, no staggered butt joints, no board-to-board value change, no sheen running away toward the door.

p_stairs.gap: The ceiling's tone is inverted. Ours is a flat mid-grey slab darker than the walls beneath it, reading as an unlit plane with four decals stuck to it. In the photograph the ceiling is the brightest surface in the frame and carries the evidence of its own fittings — a soft pool of light spreading a foot or two around each can.

p_down.gap: The treads are the wrong build entirely. Ours carpets each step wall-to-wall in flat beige with no nosing overhang and no shadow under it, so the flight reads as stacked extruded blocks. The photograph has grey plank treads with a narrow carpet runner down the centre, five inches of exposed wood either side of every step, and a crisp white skirt board raking down the wall.

p_up.gap: Held back until the stair dressing exists. Round 2 builds the newel, the black rail over white square balusters, the string, and the runner wrapping each nosing.

p_doors2.gap: The skirting has no profile and nothing to die into. Ours is a flat sliver with one chamfer, about half the height it should be, and where it reaches the door trim it merges into the casing as one undifferentiated white mass. The photograph has a five-inch board with a moulded cove cap catching light as a continuous bright ribbon, standing proud of the wall, butting into the side of a casing that stands proud of it in turn.

p_doors1.gap: The raised-panel moulding is wrong on every panel. Ours is a single flat 45° chamfer with hard mitred corners driving thirty levels of value between a blown highlight and the panel field. The real doors are moulded-skin colonial: a stepped cove with two changes of curvature, visibly rounded corners, and a panel field the same white as the stiles — the relief read from one thin bright band along each panel's top edge.

pieces.name: Knee wall
pieces.note: Carries the whole stairwell boundary now that the full-height wall behind it is gone. Thin capped pony wall, and from hallway eye level it occludes the drop — no stair treads visible from the hall.

pieces.name: Doors + casings
pieces.note: Five six-panel leaves, jamb linings, black levers, hinges, casings. Was five flat white boxes. The round-2 rewrite is on disk as doors2.py but unfinished — it renders swirl artefacts inside every panel.

pieces.name: Ceiling + lights
pieces.note: Covers the whole L, brighter than the walls now, with soft elliptical pools around each can. 2 KB over the 300 KB piece cap.

pieces.name: Baseboards
pieces.note: Runs all five edges of the L including the west alcove, which had bare wall meeting bare floor. Still lacks a moulded cove cap and a contact line at the plank.

pieces.name: Floor planks
pieces.note: The loudest open failure — five critics reached for it first, three while judging something else. Still needs plank joints, board-to-board variation and a sheen running down the hall.

pieces.name: Wall skins
pieces.note: Deleted. Two successive builders left it holding bad geometry — first a near-black panel that punched black voids into the hall, then white blobs on the west wall. The room renders on the engine's own #cfd1d2 instead, which is close to the photographs. walls3.py is on disk, unfinished.

pieces.name: Stair dressing
pieces.note: Flight, rail, runner and shaft lining all render, and the well reads to the first-floor front door. Never rebuilt: the runner should be a narrow centre band over exposed plank treads, not wall-to-wall carpet.

pieces.name: Runner + decor
pieces.note: Untouched this round. Critics judging other subjects volunteered all of it: the runner is "a lumpy melted blob", the plants "stiff extruded cactus proxies".

log.what: Stopped at the owner's call during round 2 wave A. The four in-flight builders were killed, so their partial work was reverted: the wall skin deleted again (white blobs on the west wall) and the floor restored to its previous build. The ceiling and knee wall rebuilds had already landed and were kept — both are improvements. All six views re-shot and checked.

The killed round-2 agents left three pieces placed in debug state — the knee wall in per-part R/G/B mask colours, the baseboards in magenta and the ceiling as a calibration fan — and a fourth, the wall skins, holding a near-black panel that punched two pure-black voids into the hallway above and beside the far door. All four are repaired: the real pieces re-placed, the doors reverted to the round-1 build, and the broken wall skin deleted so the room renders on the engine's own wall grey until it is rebuilt.
Those black voids had been present since round 1 and no critic caught them, because each critic was told to judge one subject. Round 2 adds two critics whose subject is the room as a whole.
Eight builders now working every verdict below, then twelve blind critics — including two judging the room as a whole rather than any one object.
Nine blind critics, nine failures, all certain. Four themes ran through every verdict: no texture anywhere, nothing touches the ground, every white is the same white, and no light falloff.

The "extra door" is answered without touching the plan. All five openings are supported by the photographs and the plan. The extra door people were seeing was a rendering artefact — every doorway carried two coincident white slabs a wall-thickness apart, ours and the neighbouring room's. That is now fixed.

Added rooms.is_void and set it on room 28 "Stairwell". house.js now skips a void room's floor slab and plinth cap, so the stairwell is a hole in the second floor instead of a slab capping it. Looking down the flight now reaches the first-floor front door.

Cut full-span floor-to-ceiling openings on room 17 edge 1 and room 28 edge 3, which makes buildRoom skip those walls outright. The full-height wall standing where the knee wall belongs is gone; the knee wall now carries the whole boundary.
Re-aimed all six cameras onto the re-traced footprint. The room's anchor had moved 3.8 ft west when its east arm was added, which left the old poses pointing at the wrong walls.
The floor plan is untouched — the polygon, the anchor and all five door positions are exactly as the owner signed them off. No other room has been modified.
